name: Kachari Ruins (Ruins of Kachari Rajbari)
description: Medieval ruins of the ancient Dimasa Kachari kingdom capital in Dimapur, featuring unique mushroom-domed sandstone pillars and V-shaped memorial stones elaborately carved with animals, birds and motifs. Protected by ASI; remnants of a pre-13th century kingdom later contested by Ahoms.
facts: Ancient capital of Dimasa Kachari kingdom before 13th century
Located near railway tracks opposite Circuit House

name: Dimapur Town
description: Largest city and commercial hub of Nagaland, known as the Gateway to Nagaland. Located on the Dhansiri River plains near the Assam border; main entry point with airport and railway station. Multi-ethnic commercial centre with markets, hotels and base for exploring the state.
facts: District headquarters and largest city in Nagaland
Only major airport and railway in the state

name: Nagaland Science Centre
description: Interactive science museum and educational centre behind Naga Shopping Arcade in Half Nagarjan, Dimapur. Features galleries on senses, children's corner, fun science, planetarium and science park. Established with NCSM support to promote scientific awareness.

name: NEZCC Stone Garden and North East Heritage Museum
description: North East Zone Cultural Centre complex near Dimapur Airport featuring a stone sculpture garden with 31 works by Indian artists, traditional morungs, amphitheatre and the North East Heritage Museum showcasing crafts and artefacts from eight northeastern states.
facts: About 3 km from railway station, near airport
Stone garden and museum open to public
Average footfall 20 daily, higher on weekends

name: Hong Kong Market
description: Bustling flea market in central Dimapur known for affordable imported clothing, footwear, electronics and daily goods from Myanmar, Thailand and China. Popular shopping destination for locals and tourists; evolved from Tibetan traders' stalls in the 1980s.

name: Green Park
description: Family-oriented park inside the State Horticulture Nursery at 4th Mile, Dimapur. Features greenery, boating, water zorbing, ziplining, kids' train and picnic spots. Popular local hangout and tourist attraction.

name: Heirloom Naga Centre
description: Creative hub near Seluphe Junction, Sovima Village area showcasing contemporary and traditional Naga crafts, brands, gallery, workshops and experiential tourism. Unites local artisan brands under one roof.
facts: Near Sovima, about 15 min from airport

name: Zhotomi Ce (Naga United Village)
description: Traditional Chakhesang Naga house and living museum of artist Veswuzo Phesao in Naga United Village area. Features classic Kunemeche architecture with carved wood, mithun heads, and cultural displays; recipient of Governor's Award.
facts: Wood carvings of warriors and symbols

name: Kohima Town
description: Capital of Nagaland and headquarters of Kohima district, a hill city at about 1,444 m elevation known for its role in World War II and as base for exploring Naga culture, war sites, and nearby valleys.
facts: Base for Hornbill Festival and Dzukou trek

name: Kohima War Cemetery
description: Commonwealth War Graves Commission cemetery on Garrison Hill in central Kohima, commemorating 1,420 Allied soldiers who died in the 1944 Battle of Kohima. Features the famous epitaph and preserved tennis court site of fierce fighting.
facts: Famous epitaph: When you go home tell them of us and say for your tomorrow we gave our today
Located on the battlefield of Garrison Hill

name: Kisama Heritage Village
description: Naga Heritage Village 12 km south of Kohima, designed as a traditional Naga village with morungs representing all ethnic groups. Permanent venue of the annual Hornbill Festival showcasing Naga culture, crafts, and performances.
facts: Name from Kigwema and Phesama villages
About 12 km from Kohima on NH

name: Khonoma Green Village
description: Western Angami Naga village 20 km west of Kohima, India's first green village with community conservation, terraced fields, and the Khonoma Nature Conservation and Tragopan Sanctuary protecting Blyth's Tragopan. Historic site of resistance against British.
facts: Home to Khonoma Nature Conservation and Tragopan Sanctuary

name: Dzukou Valley
description: High-altitude valley at about 2,438-2,452 m on the Kohima (Nagaland)-Senapati (Manipur) border, known for rolling meadows, dwarf bamboo, seasonal wildflowers including the Dzukou Lily, and popular moderate treks from Viswema or Jakhama.
facts: Known for Dzukou Lily and meadows
Trek from Viswema or Jakhama villages

name: Japfu Peak
description: Second highest peak in Nagaland at 3,048 m in Kohima district, about 15 km south of Kohima. Popular moderate trek from Kigwema; holds Guinness record for tallest rhododendron tree and offers views over Dzukou Valley.
facts: Elevation 3,048 m, second highest in Nagaland
Guinness record for tallest rhododendron tree
Views of Dzukou Valley and surrounding hills

name: Nagaland State Museum
description: State museum at Bayavu Hill in Kohima displaying traditional Naga clothing, ornaments, weapons, musical instruments, artworks, and models of tribal houses across multiple galleries.

name: Mary Help of Christians Cathedral
description: Large modern cathedral in Kohima, considered one of the biggest in Northeast India, known for its architecture and as a major Christian landmark in the predominantly Christian state.
facts: One of the largest cathedrals in the Northeast

name: Dzüleke Village
description: Scenic Angami village near Kohima known for its traditional setting, surrounding forests, and as a quieter offbeat alternative for experiencing rural Naga life and nature walks.
facts: Near Kohima, accessible for day visits

name: Touphema Tourist Village
description: Community-run tourist village about 40 km from Kohima offering homestays, cultural experiences, and model for rural tourism among Naga tribes.
